frontmatter.title: MiTHo: access and interpret Cumulative Hazard Indices
frontmatter.subject: Hackathon Notebooks

children.value: Explore re-projected dataset in the Med cube
This dataset provides monthly information on Cumulative Hazard Indexs (CHIs) at the sea surface (3D, lat, lon, time) at global scale. The dataset is split into 3 zarr stores:

This tutorial accesses the published Zarr stores over HTTPS and illustrates the
multistressor construction of CHI1, global July 2022 conditions, and annual changes across
the Mediterranean and four subbasins: Western Mediterranean, Adriatic, Ionian,
and Levantine–Aegean. The monthly map shows July 2022; time series cover the full record.

The Mediterranean is used here as a regional example to illustrate basin-scale and subbasin-scale analyses.
A global map provides context; basin analyses are examples, not a geographic restriction of the data.
Sea surface temperature (SST): warm and cold extremes; hydrogen ion concentration (H+): acidification
Temperature: warm and cold extremes; dissolved oxygen: deoxygenation; salinity: low and high extremes
SST, H+, sea surface salinity (SSS), sea surface density (SSD), wind speed: nine stressors in total
SST: warm and cold extremes; fishing effort (FE): high values
The dataset is gridded on a 1° x 1° regular lat-lon grid.

Geographic coverage and valid-data masks differ between indices.
CHI3 combines both low and high extremes of SSS, SSD and wind in a single index.
For any given variable and threshold pair, low and high extremes are mutually exclusive
at the same place and time. Extremes of different variables can occur together.

distributed with this
notebook. The notebook reads it without modifying it; it does not create,
resample or export a basin-mask file. No original high-resolution masks are needed.
The input path can be changed in the settings below.
Figures, tables and run information are saved in

.
Access to the public CHI data requires internet. Cartopy may also download
Natural Earth coastline and land files on the first run.

# Libraries for arrays, remote data, tables and maps.
from pathlib import Path
import importlib.metadata as metadata
import json
import urllib.request
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import xarray as xr
import dask
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.colors as mcolors
from matplotlib.patches import Patch
import cartopy
import cartopy.crs as ccrs
import cartopy.feature as cfeature
from IPython.display import display
Create the output directory and display the package versions used for this run.

# Keep generated files together; do not modify the source data.
ARTIFACTS = Path("notebook_artifacts")
ARTIFACTS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
cartopy.config["data_dir"] = ARTIFACTS / "cartopy_data"

    "numpy",
    "xarray",
    "zarr",
    "fsspec",
    "aiohttp",
    "dask",
    "matplotlib",
    "cartopy",
]
versions = {name: metadata.version(name) for name in packages}
display(pd.Series(versions, name="Installed version").to_frame())
assert (
    int(versions["zarr"].split(".")[0]) >= 3
), "Install the supplied Zarr 3 environment."

children.value: The original processing code constructs the unnormalized CHI1 as:

the acidification contribution. They are non-negative, dimensionless
stressor intensities derived from standardized anomalies at detected extremes.
They are
not raw SST or pH measurements

. For SST, the processing uses monthly
90th/10th percentile thresholds for warm/cold extremes, respectively.
The example uses the unnormalized, fixed-climatology variables.

identifies
the alternative based on a moving climatology, rather than simply a smoothed CHI
time series.

they are not interchangeable with the variables plotted here.

divides the raw index by the global spatial maximum of each month.
The global context below uses

# Names and example settings can be changed here.
VARIABLES = ["CH1_CHI1", "CH1_S_MHW", "CH1_S_CS", "CH1_S_PH"]
LABELS = [
    "CHI1 — cumulative index",
    "Marine heatwave contribution",
    "Cold-spell contribution",
    "Acidification contribution",
]
assert set(VARIABLES).issubset(ds.data_vars)
assert all(ds[v].dims == ("time", "latitude", "longitude") for v in VARIABLES)

DATE = "2022-07"
MASK_FILE = Path("inputs/mediterranean_subbasin_masks_1deg.nc")
LON_BOUNDS = (-6.062, 36.06)
LAT_BOUNDS = (30.27, 45.98)
A small helper keeps geographic slicing valid for either coordinate ordering.
Select only the variables and geographic rectangle needed for the regional example.

# Selection is still lazy; no numerical arrays are loaded yet.
subset = ds[DYNAMIC_VARIABLES].sel(
    longitude=coordinate_slice(ds.longitude, LON_BOUNDS),
    latitude=coordinate_slice(ds.latitude, LAT_BOUNDS),
)
assert subset.sizes["latitude"] > 0 and subset.sizes["longitude"] > 0
print("Native chunks:", {v: ds[v].encoding.get("chunks") for v in VARIABLES})
print("Subset dimensions:", dict(subset.sizes))

# Read only these five variables, with bounded concurrent chunk decompression.
# Native chunks are large: a small map/point may still require substantial I/O.
Load the selected regional data once, then extract the July 2022 map.

# Limit concurrent decompression because the native chunks are large.
with dask.config.set(scheduler="threads", num_workers=2):
    regional = subset.compute()

selected_month = regional.sel(time=DATE)
assert selected_month.sizes["time"] == 1, "Expected one monthly sample."
snapshot = selected_month.isel(time=0, drop=True)

This retains the spatial contrast between places with no detected stressors and

The colour scale covers the actual minimum of zero to the maximum in this map;

children.value:
All panels use the same linear colour scale so the magnitude of the contributions
can be compared directly. Land is grey; missing marine values are left blank.
Only Mediterranean grid-cell centres selected by the geographic mask below are plotted.
The basin time series below use these four subbasins and their union.

# A common scale allows direct magnitude comparisons between the four panels.
values = snapshot[VARIABLES].to_array().values
finite_values = values[np.isfinite(values)]
assert finite_values.size > 0
vmax = float(finite_values.max())
norm = mcolors.Normalize(vmin=0, vmax=max(vmax, 1e-12))
cmap = plt.colormaps["viridis"].copy()
cmap.set_bad("white")
Draw the cumulative index and its components with the same colour limits.

# Use the same date, grid and geographic mask in every panel.
fig, axes = plt.subplots(
    2,
    2,
    figsize=(13, 6),
    subplot_kw={"projection": ccrs.PlateCarree()},
    layout="constrained",
)
for ax, variable, label in zip(axes.flat, VARIABLES, LABELS):
    field = snapshot[variable]
    mesh = ax.pcolormesh(
        field.longitude,
        field.latitude,
        field,
        transform=ccrs.PlateCarree(),
        shading="auto",
        cmap=cmap,
        norm=norm,
    )
    ax.set_extent([*LON_BOUNDS, *LAT_BOUNDS], crs=ccrs.PlateCarree())
    ax.add_feature(cfeature.LAND.with_scale("110m"), facecolor="0.85", zorder=3)
    ax.coastlines(resolution="110m", linewidth=0.6, zorder=4)
    gl = ax.gridlines(draw_labels=True, linewidth=0.3, alpha=0.4)
    gl.top_labels = False
    gl.right_labels = False
    ax.set_title(label, fontsize=11)
fig.colorbar(
    mesh,
    ax=list(axes.flat),
    label="Dimensionless index / stressor contribution",
    shrink=0.85,
    pad=0.03,
)
fig.suptitle(f"MiTHo CHI1 and component stressors — {DATE}", fontsize=15)

children.value:
Use the same spatial sample in every month: only cells with finite CHI1,
normalized CHI1 and all three contributions throughout 1993–2022 are retained.
Weights are proportional to

. Missing areas are not filled or
extrapolated. The coverage table reports how much of each CHI marine footprint
is retained. Subbasin means use the supplied boundaries, not rectangular selections.

Each panel shows basin-mean CHI1 and its three contributions, on a common y scale.
The dashed line marks July 2022. All 360 monthly samples are shown without smoothing.

# Keep the same complete-data cells throughout the record.
all_complete = (
    np.isfinite(regional[DYNAMIC_VARIABLES].to_array("variable"))
    .all("variable")
    .all("time")
)
lat_weights = np.cos(np.deg2rad(regional.latitude)).broadcast_like(med_mask)
coverage_rows, basin_weights, basin_monthly_fields = [], {}, {}
monthly_frames = []
Compute one area-weighted monthly series per basin for each variable.

# Cosine latitude weights account for cell-area differences on the regular grid.
for name, mask in basin_masks.items():
    retained = mask & all_complete
    assert int(retained.sum()) > 0, f"No complete cells in {name}"
    w = lat_weights.where(retained, 0)
    basin_weights[name] = w
    fields = regional[VARIABLES].weighted(w).mean(("latitude", "longitude"))
    basin_monthly_fields[name] = fields
    coverage_rows.append(
        {
            "Basin": name,
            "CHI marine grid cells": int(mask.sum()),
            "Retained complete cells": int(retained.sum()),
            "Retained area fraction (%)": float(
                100 * w.sum() / lat_weights.where(mask, 0).sum()
            ),
        }
    )
    frame = fields.to_dataframe()[VARIABLES].reset_index()
    frame.insert(0, "Basin", name)
    monthly_frames.append(frame)
Inspect the retained coverage before interpreting the basin means.

# Export the series and coverage so the numerical results can be inspected.
coverage_table = pd.DataFrame(coverage_rows)
display(coverage_table.round(2))
coverage_table.to_csv(ARTIFACTS / "basin_coverage.csv", index=False)
pd.concat(monthly_frames, ignore_index=True).to_csv(
    ARTIFACTS / "basin_monthly_series.csv", index=False
)

8. Basin-wide annual evolution: are recent extremes stronger or more frequent?

children.label: 8. Basin-wide annual evolution: are recent extremes stronger or more frequent?

children.value: same spatial sample in every month

: retain basin grid cells with finite
CHI1, normalized CHI1 and all three contributions for all 360 months.
Use weights proportional to

for the equal-angle grid. The coverage
table reports the retained fraction of each geographic mask; results describe those
observed cells, not an extrapolation to missing parts of the basin.
mean over retained basin cells and all months of each year, including zeros.
annual mean of the monthly area fraction satisfying
annual weighted mean raw CHI1 across the active cell-months only.

The last metric helps separate magnitude from occurrence. An increase in mean CHI1
alone does not establish that individual extremes became stronger. These are descriptive
comparisons under a fixed-climatology index, not a trend-significance or attribution test.

# Aggregate the monthly data by calendar year; active intensity excludes inactive cell-months.
annual_rows, decade_rows = [], []
basin_monthly = {}
for name, mask in basin_masks.items():
    w = basin_weights[name]
    retained = w > 0
    total_w = w.sum()
    field = regional.CH1_CHI1.where(retained)
    active = (regional.CH1_CHI1_norm > 1e-4) & retained
    monthly_mean = field.weighted(w).mean(("latitude", "longitude"))
    active_weight = w.where(active, 0).sum(("latitude", "longitude"))
    active_sum = (field.where(active, 0) * w).sum(("latitude", "longitude"))
    monthly_fraction = 100 * active_weight / total_w
    annual_mean = monthly_mean.resample(time="YS").mean()
    annual_area = monthly_fraction.resample(time="YS").mean()
    annual_intensity = (
        active_sum.resample(time="YS").sum() / active_weight.resample(time="YS").sum()
    )
    basin_monthly[name] = {
        "mean": monthly_mean,
        "area": monthly_fraction,
        "active_sum": active_sum,
        "active_weight": active_weight,
    }
    for i, time in enumerate(annual_mean.time.values):
        annual_rows.append(
            {
                "Basin": name,
                "Year": pd.Timestamp(time).year,
                "Mean CHI1": float(annual_mean[i]),
                "Affected area (%)": float(annual_area[i]),
                "Intensity when active": float(annual_intensity[i]),
            }
        )
    for label, start, end in [
        ("1993–2002", "1993", "2002"),
        ("2013–2022", "2013", "2022"),
    ]:
        s = slice(start, end)
        decade_rows.append(
            {
                "Basin": name,
                "Period": label,
                "Mean CHI1": float(monthly_mean.sel(time=s).mean()),
                "Affected area (%)": float(monthly_fraction.sel(time=s).mean()),
                "Intensity when active": float(
                    active_sum.sel(time=s).sum() / active_weight.sel(time=s).sum()
                ),
            }
        )

All maps cover the full 1993–2022 period:

The 1.001 upper bound is the numerical margin used in the source code; the nominal
normalized upper limit is 1. Category is relative to each month’s global spatial maximum,
not an absolute hazard threshold. Categories partition positive normalized values;
their total can differ from PI because PI excludes values at or below

These full-period counts locate repeated occurrence but do not themselves show
whether events increased towards the end of the record. Use the annual metrics above
for that question. Maps below retain the same complete-data Mediterranean mask.
Each panel has its own colour scale in months, to make the rarer high category visible;
compare the colourbar values, not colours alone, between panels.

# Load the supplied full-period count maps only when they are needed.
STATIC_VARIABLES = ["CH1_CHI1_PI", "CH1_CHI1_Cat"]
with dask.config.set(scheduler="threads", num_workers=2):
    static_region = (
        ds[STATIC_VARIABLES]

        .compute()

Check that the supplied counts agree with the monthly normalized index.

# Count months, not consecutive duration; preserve the original category thresholds.
norm_series = regional.CH1_CHI1_norm
computed_pi = (norm_series > 1e-4).sum("time")
pi = static_region.CH1_CHI1_PI
np.testing.assert_allclose(
    pi.values[retained_med.values], computed_pi.values[retained_med.values]
)
category = static_region.CH1_CHI1_Cat
assert category.sizes["intensity_class"] == 3
category_ranges = [(0, 0.33), (0.33, 0.66), (0.66, 1.001)]
for i, (lower, upper) in enumerate(category_ranges):
    recomputed = ((norm_series > lower) & (norm_series <= upper)).sum("time")
    stored = category.isel(intensity_class=i)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        stored.values[retained_med.values], recomputed.values[retained_med.values]
    )
print(
    "Stored PI and all three Category counts match monthly data on the retained Mediterranean mask."
)
